120	Remember I said that the word "this day" is mentioned here
121	once, and here too: "and HaShem has declared you this day."
122	So let's start with the Ramban, who begins by explaining the "day":
123	"And HaShem has declared you this day" — for this day is for you like the day of
124	Sinai,
125	like the day of Sinai, and HaShem has exalted you and raised you through the receiving of
126	the Torah, that you be for Him a treasured people from among all the nations, for only
127	you received the Torah.
128	So there is a correspondence between these two days: the day of
129	the giving of the Torah at Mount Sinai and this day.
130	I'll try to briefly go back over something we spoke
131	about in the past, in Parashat Bechukotai,
132	and in past years also here in Parashat Ki Tavo. A very
133	important point.
134	At Mount Sinai,
135	we will see in a moment the verses describing
136	the scene at Mount Sinai, or what happened before the giving of the Torah,
137	the Holy One, blessed be He, offers us the Torah through
138	Moshe Rabbeinu,
139	and we said "we will do and we will hear," and we meant it.
140	But as is known, 40 days after the giving of the Torah
141	there was the sin of the golden calf,
142	and we did not receive the Torah, meaning we did not receive
143	in practice the tablets; they were broken on the seventeenth of Tammuz.
144	Now there were two covenants: there was a covenant that was sealed
145	at Sinai,
146	and another covenant at the end of the 40 years, in the Plains of Moav.
147	In the continuation of this parashah, Parashat Ki Tavo, in fact
148	this is the center of Parashat Ki Tavo, but since
149	we spoke about this in past years, I won't go back
150	over it now. The center of the parashah is the rebuke,
151	the section of the rebuke, right: if you listen to its commandments,
152	it will be thus, and if you do not listen, it will be otherwise. And it is written
153	there at the end:
154	"These are the words of the covenant which HaShem commanded Moshe to make with the children of Israel
155	in the land of Moav, besides the covenant which He made with them
156	at Sinai." So there were two covenants, and the question is why two
157	covenants are needed. The answer, as we said: the first covenant
158	was broken.
